title.narrative: Public Expenditures for Administrative Capacity Endurance (PEACE) in Ukraine

description.narrative: The Project consists of the following parts:Part 1. Supporting the Recipient in: (a) maintaining core government functions through: (i) the payment of Salaries of Eligible Employees; and (ii) the payment of Salaries of Eligible Higher Education Institutions Employees; and (b) the provision of Project audits.Part 2. Supporting the Recipient in: (a) financing monthly pension payments subsidized by the central government; and (b) maintaining its social assistance systems and programs through financing of:- the GMI Program, which provides monthly benefits to low-income families;- the HUS Program, which provides financial support to low-income families and individuals for the payment of utility bills;- the Disability Program, which provides financial support to eligible persons with disabilities;- the IDP Program, which provides monthly cash allowances to eligible IDPs; and- the Family with Children Programs, which provide support to Eligible Families with Children.Part 3. Supporting the Recipient in maintaining: (a) health care services delivery under the PMG through the financing of PMG Payments to Eligible Health Service Providers in order to pay salaries of healthcare workers; and (b) emergency service delivery through the payment of Salaries of Eligible First Responders.The Project and AF1 had one component, focusing on reimbursement of salaries of core government and school employees. Under AF2, Project activities expanded with two new components: component 2 focused on reimbursement of pensions and expenditures under social assistance programs and component 3 focused on reimbursement of healthcare workers and first responders salaries. Under AF3, Project activities remained the same. Under AF4, Project activities further expanded to include higher education employees salaries and family and child benefits. AF8 was approved on December 21, 2024, and changed the Project cost to US$56,047 million. AFs 2-8 provided for financing gaps that allowed the PEACE operation to absorb additional donor contributions as they became available. AF8 created an initial financing gap of US$5,000 million. This financing gap has been partially filled by a grant of US$691 million approved by the ECAVP on February 3, 2026.The Project Operational Manual, updated following each AF, defines responsibilities, eligibility criteria, and detailed procedures related to implementation of the Project and AFs in line with all applicable Bank policies.
To contribute to sustaining the government administrative and service delivery capacity to exercise core government functions at the national and regional levels
